text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 reporting year, the Harrowmere Household Resilience Fund delivered monthly cash transfers to 4,812 households across the Kelvane and Dunsmoor districts. Each household received the equivalent of 38 dollars per month, paid through mobile wallets on the fifth working day. Endline surveys found that 71% of recipient households ate at least two meals a day, compared with 49% at baseline. Transfers were not conditional on school attendance or clinic visits, which reduced the administrative burden on field staff. Seven distribution points were closed after flooding in March, but no household missed more than one payment. We are grateful to the Linden Trust for its continued support and flexibility.

passages.source_passage: In the 2022-23 school year, the Sahelia Bright Plates Initiative served hot midday meals in 36 primary schools across the Toumbara region. Cooks prepared a millet and cowpea dish fortified with iron, reaching an average of 9,400 pupils each school day. Head teachers reported that attendance rose by 14% in the first two terms. The meals were not served during the eight-week lean season closure, because roads to eleven schools became impassable. Parent committees supplied firewood and water, and volunteer mothers supervised every kitchen. We did not record any food safety incidents during the year. Your grant covered roughly 60 percent of commodity costs, with the remainder sourced from local farmers' cooperatives.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Corrin Gate Skills Centre opened its welding and solar installation tracks in January 2024. Since then, 112 trainees have enrolled, of whom 87 completed the full sixteen-week course. Six months after graduation, 58 percent of completers were in paid work or running their own small enterprises. The centre has not yet secured accreditation from the national vocational authority, and the inspection visit was postponed twice. Female enrolment remains low at one in five trainees, despite targeted outreach in Pell Market. Management proposes that the board approve a second intake of 60 trainees in September, funded from the reserve.

passages.source_passage: The Ostrel Lane Evening Literacy Network was founded in 2015 by three retired teachers in the market town of Brenmoor. It now runs 24 evening classes in church halls, mosques and community centres, each meeting twice a week for ninety minutes. A 2023 household survey commissioned by the district council estimated that 31% of adults in Brenmoor cannot read a simple bus timetable. Most of our learners are women aged between 30 and 55 who never completed primary school. Existing government provision does not reach outlying villages after dark, when most adults have finished work. This proposal seeks support to open ten new classes and to train 40 volunteer facilitators over two years.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation covers the first eighteen months of the Little Lanterns Playgroup Network, which operates 42 playgroups in the Fenwick Hills. Evaluators observed 30 sessions and interviewed 126 caregivers between May and July 2024. Children attending at least twice weekly scored 12% higher on the Fenwick early learning checklist than a comparison group. Caregivers valued the songs and storytelling but said the venues were often cold in winter. Facilitators had not received refresher training since their induction, and several reported uncertainty about recording developmental milestones. The evaluation did not find evidence that fathers' participation had increased. We recommend a revised training schedule and a modest heating budget for the remaining period.

passages.source_passage: Before your first community drill, make sure every household on your list knows the three warning signals used by the Saltreach Early Warning Committee. One long siren blast means prepare, two short blasts mean move to high ground, and a continuous tone means the danger has passed. Volunteers should never tell residents to wait for a second warning before leaving. In the 2021 cyclone drill, only 64% of households in Marrow Point reached the assembly site within twenty minutes. Walk the evacuation route yourself at least once a month. If a family has an elderly or disabled member, note this on the register; do not assume neighbours will help without being asked.

passages.source_passage: In 2023 the Greywater Valley Farmer Field Schools network grew from 18 to 27 schools, each with about 25 members meeting fortnightly on a shared demonstration plot. Participants tested drought-tolerant sorghum alongside their usual maize varieties. Average sorghum yields on demonstration plots reached 1.4 tonnes per hectare, nearly double the district average. Rains failed in October, and maize plots did not produce a harvestable crop in four of the schools. Members adopted mulching on an estimated 340 hectares of their own land. Women made up 62 percent of participants, although none of the schools was yet chaired by a woman. We thank the Ashby Foundation for funding seed, tools and facilitator stipends.

passages.source_passage: The Kestrel Bay Savings Groups programme now supports 156 village savings and loan associations, up from 120 at the last board meeting. Total member savings reached 2.3 million shillings in the quarter ending June 2024. The average loan was used for small trading, school fees or livestock purchases. Repayment rates stayed above 95 percent in all but three groups. The programme did not provide any external capital to the groups, which continue to lend only from their own savings. Two groups in Torrin Ward dissolved after disputes over share-out, and staff were not able to mediate in time. We ask the board to note the planned expansion into Lowfield sub-county.

passages.source_passage: Each caregiver volunteer in the Amberline Home Care Programme is assigned between six and ten households and should visit each one at least once a week. During a visit, check that the client has taken their antiretroviral medicine and has at least a seven-day supply remaining. Never discuss a client's HIV status with neighbours or relatives unless the client has given permission. Record each visit on the green card within 24 hours. In 2022, volunteers identified 38 clients who had stopped treatment, and most resumed within a month after a referral. If a client is too weak to stand, do not attempt to lift them alone; call your supervisor.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers July to December 2024 for the Mirambo District Community Health Worker Programme. A total of 214 community health workers were active during the period, against a target of 240. Together they conducted 18,650 household visits and referred 1,132 children with danger signs to health facilities. Stock-outs of amoxicillin were reported in 9 of 31 villages in October. Supervisors did not complete the planned monthly supportive supervision visits in Kilembe ward, where two posts were vacant. Data from the mobile reporting app showed that 83% of visits were logged on the same day. No maternal deaths were recorded among households visited by community health workers during the period.
